_comment: Screening universe for the daily sweep. THE definition of what gets looked at before any idea is written: a GLOBAL core of index constituents (Tier 1), every name the books hold (Tier 2), and a hand-curated thematic watchlist (Tier 3) - plus an index/sector dislocation screen that runs above the single-name layer. Read by screen_universe.py (produces the candidate list) and by build_today_focus.py (validates that every single-name idea declares a tier). Hand-edit Tier 3 and the index list only; Tier 1 constituents are fetched and Tier 2 is derived.
note_on_market_cap: There is deliberately NO single market-cap floor. Cap spans ~50x inside the intended universe (a low-tens-of-billions optical name vs a few-hundred-million substrate name), so any floor either admits several thousand names or excludes the thematic tier outright. Membership and intent are the gates; marketCapBn is RECORDED on every single-name idea as a sourced descriptor, never used as the filter.

core.label: Tier 1 - Core index constituents (global)
core.definition: The union of the constituent sets of every index listed in `indices` below. Global by design - US, Europe, UK and Asia are all first-class.
core.why_not_stored: Index membership changes with every rebalance, and a hand-typed list of ~2,000 global tickers would be an unsourced assertion - the one thing this repo bans everywhere else. screen_universe.py fetches each constituent set and stamps provenance + asOf; the fetched snapshot is committed as universe.constituents.json so any sweep is reproducible.
sources: Second independent constituent source required before the snapshot is committed - the same >=2-source rule the sweep runs on
core.approxCount: ~2,000-2,600 unique names depending on overlap and the Korea decision below
core.screen: Rank by % off 52-week high within each region, apply the >~15% dislocation rule, then cap the candidate list (see screenOutput). Market cap is recorded on every candidate, never used to filter.

indices.note: Heavy overlap with SPX; ~35-40 names are NDX-only.

indices.note: Explicitly requested. A sector index and a subset of SXXP; doubles as an index-level dislocation signal for European financials.

indices.note: Added for genuine European breadth - 50 names cannot carry 'scan Europe'. Supersets SX5E and SX7E, and reaches Swiss/Nordic listings the euro indices miss.

indices.note: The books hold SHEL LN and DGE LN; UK is named in the sweep coverage spec but had no universe behind it.

indices.name: Korea Composite
indices.note: Explicitly requested. See koreaBreadthDecision - the full board carries a long illiquid tail the liquidity floor filters.

indices.name: Nikkei 225
indices.note: The yen complex is a standing desk theme; Japan equity had no universe behind it.

indices.name: Taiwan Weighted

indices.name: Hang Seng
indices.note: China/HK exposure; the China overhang already drives AMAT-type theses.

core.koreaBreadthDecision: Requested as 'all stocks in KOSPI'. The full board is ~800 listings with a long illiquid tail. Rather than narrow it to KOSPI 200 - which would silently drop names - the full board is scanned and the Tier 1 liquidity floor filters the tail. Set coreBreadth to 'kospi200' if you would rather cut it at the index level instead.
core.liquidityRule: PROPOSED, override freely. A ~$10m 20-day average dollar volume floor applied when building the CANDIDATE list only - it never blocks an idea you choose to write. Without it a global ~2,400-name union in a drawdown tape returns several hundred >15% hits and the sweep drowns. A noise filter, not a suitability rule.
core.fxNote: Non-US constituents quote in local currency. marketCapBn and advUsdM must be normalised to USD at the scan date and the rate recorded, or the numbers are not comparable across regions.

held.label: Tier 2 - Held names
held.definition: Every listed position across the nine client books in data.js that is not already in Tier 1.
held.why: Makes 'widely-held' literal instead of a judgment call, and is the only tier that catches non-US listings clients actually own. Cannot drift from the books because it is computed from them.
held.screen: Same dislocation rule as Tier 1, plus any position sitting on an unrealised loss or a concentration breach flagged by scanner.js.
held.note_on_global: Now largely a subset of Tier 1 once SXXP and UKX are in - ASML NA, SAP GY, SHEL LN, DGE LN and TTE FP are all index members. Tier 2 stays a distinct tier because it is DERIVED from the books and so cannot drift, and because it catches any future holding outside the indices.

thematic.label: Tier 3 - Thematic watchlist
thematic.definition: Deliberately hand-curated names outside the indices, tracked because the desk wants coverage ahead of the street.
thematic.why_curated: This is the tier where the desk is front-running coverage. Membership is a judgment call by design and must not be derivable from anything.
thematic.liquidityRule: Below ~$5m 20-day average dollar volume the build WARNS and the idea must state a maximum position size; it still ships. Keeps genuinely early names reachable while forcing the sizing conversation into the open rather than leaving it implicit.
thematic.convictionRule: Tier 3 ideas carry speculative:true and can never label High regardless of raw pillar score. Thin sell-side coverage and thin liquidity are real reasons to hold conviction back, and the existing consensus pillar cannot be honestly sourced for a two-analyst name.
thematic.derivativesRule: Direct equity is a legitimate primary expression for this tier. Listed options on these names are thin or absent (a Stockholm listing has no US-listed options at all), so the derivatives-first principle is relaxed here rather than satisfied with a construction that could not actually be executed.

photonics.label: Photonics / optical networking
photonics.rationale: AI datacenter interconnect - the optical layer behind the capex cycle the desk already covers on the compute side.

names.name: Sivers Semiconductors
names.note: Confirmed as the Stockholm listing (Sivers Semiconductors AB), not a US ticker. Consequences: no US-listed options, so direct equity is the only expression - which the Tier 3 derivatives-first relaxation already permits; and a SEK-quoted line carries currency exposure for a USD- or EUR-base book, so any idea on it must state whether the FX is hedged.

photonics.livenessCheck: REQUIRED before first scan. Several classic photonics tickers were acquired or wound down (Infinera, NeoPhotonics, EMCORE) and are deliberately absent. screen_universe.py must report any ticker the scanner cannot resolve rather than silently skipping it.

thematic.venueNote: A Tier 3 name may list anywhere - the cohort is curated on the theme, not the exchange. Each name therefore carries `venue` and `scanRegion` so screen_universe.py can resolve it on the right endpoint. A non-US listing usually means no US-listed options, which is exactly why this tier relaxes derivatives-first; it also means FX exposure that an idea must address.

recordedFields.tier: REQUIRED on every single-name idea: core | held | thematic. Macro ideas (FX, rates, commodities, index) use tier 'macro' and are exempt from every tier rule below.
recordedFields.marketCapBn: REQUIRED on every single-name idea, sourced from the scanner (market_cap_basic), not authored. A descriptor, not a gate.
recordedFields.advUsdM: REQUIRED on Tier 3 ideas: 20-day average dollar volume, sourced from the scanner.
recordedFields.speculative: Auto-set true for Tier 3 by the generator; caps the conviction label at Medium.
recordedFields.maxPositionBps: REQUIRED on a Tier 3 idea that trips the soft liquidity floor.

indexAndSectorScreen._comment: Above the single-name layer. Indices and sector baskets are screenable objects in their own right - a sector index 20% off its high is a candidate thesis even when no single constituent stands out, and it is how a European-banks or semis dislocation gets surfaced as one idea rather than twelve.
indexAndSectorScreen.screen: % off 52-week high, 1-week and 1-month move, and dispersion vs the parent index.

watch.name: Russell 2000
watch.note: Breadth/rotation read - already quoted in the weekly letter.

watch.name: Korea Composite
watch.note: Memory-cycle read - the SK Hynix/Samsung tape already drives MU theses.

indexAndSectorScreen.ideaTier: An index- or sector-level idea is tier 'macro' - no marketCapBn or liquidity obligation.
indexAndSectorScreen.screenVsExpress: The object SCREENED and the instrument TRADED are different things, deliberately. Screen the INDEX (SXEP, the GICS sector level) because it is the cleaner signal - pure sector, no fee drag, no tracking error, longer history. Express via the tradable PROXY (XLE, the corresponding sector UCITS ETF, or a basket of constituents) because an index cannot be bought. The idea records the index as `ticker` and the proxy in `structures` / `preferredExpression`, exactly as a single-name idea records the underlying and its option.
indexAndSectorScreen.howSectorIdeasMap: A sector idea routes through mapping.js BETTER than a single name, because idea.sector is precisely what two of the four fit axes key on. Affinity fit reads the book's allocation to that sector against its 24-month history and the comfort peg; Gap fit reads the sector's goal bucket (SECTOR_BUCKET: Energy/Utilities/Real Estate/Infrastructure -> Income, Gold -> Preservation, Crypto -> Growth) against the derived goal target. Same signal as a single name, minus the idiosyncratic risk. Every sector index below therefore declares `appSector`, which MUST be one of the sectors already used in data.js or the idea cannot be scored.
indexAndSectorScreen.sectorIdeaIntent: An overweight book is not a reason to skip a sector - it is a reason to change the INTENT. Energy today: Ben sits at 23% (XOM 13 + SHEL 10) against the 15% Income comfort peg, so an intent 'add' idea correctly scores near-dead for him (8pp overshoot = an 80-point Affinity penalty, and no gap headroom), while intent 'protect' or 'trim' - collar the block, overwrite it - is exactly right. Amar (8%) and Aurora (4.3%) have headroom and take the 'add'. One sector dislocation can therefore legitimately produce two ideas with opposite intents.

sectorIndices.verifyOnFirstScan: Index codes and proxy tickers below MUST be resolved against the scanner before the first live run; anything unresolved is REPORTED, never silently skipped. European sector ETF proxies are deliberately left unnamed - the ticker varies by provider and listing venue (Xetra / LSE / Milan) and must be resolved at scan time rather than asserted here.

asia.family: Not covered at sector level in v3.
asia.why: Korea, Japan and Taiwan sector indices are fragmented across exchange-specific families with no clean cross-market equivalent to GICS or STOXX supersectors, and there is no reliable UCITS/US-listed sector proxy for most of them. Asia is screened at INDEX level (KOSPI, NKY, TWSE, HSI) and at SINGLE-NAME level via Tier 1, which already catches the memory-cycle and semi-supply-chain reads that matter to this desk. Revisit if an Asia sector thesis needs an expression the index level cannot carry.

indexAndSectorScreen.tradabilityGap: KNOWN GAP, not yet modelled. mapping.js tradability() only tests OTC-vs-structured against MiFID classification. It does NOT know that a US-listed ETF (XLE and every SPDR proxy above) generally cannot be distributed to an EU retail client without a PRIIPs KID - which would bite on Aurora (MiFID Retail, EUR base). Today a US sector-ETF idea would show as tradable for her when in practice it is not. Either add a domicile check to tradability(), or require the European proxy on any sector idea flagged to an EU retail book.

screenOutput._comment: What screen_universe.py hands the sweep. Bounded on purpose - an unbounded global candidate list is the same as no screen at all.
screenOutput.artifact: universe.candidates.json (committed each sweep, so the run is reproducible)
screenOutput.rank: Primary: % off 52-week high. Ties broken by dollar volume, so a widely-traded dislocation outranks a thin one.
alwaysInclude: Every Tier 2 held name that trips the dislocation rule, uncapped - clients own these.
Every Tier 3 name, uncapped - the watchlist is small and curated by hand.
screenOutput.reportUnresolved: Any ticker the scanner cannot resolve is REPORTED, never silently skipped (same rule as tv_technicals.py).
